title: census leak_problems passes a new source row whose url carries user:password@, because kbpublic.file_hits strips urls and only an email is checked in the raw url
goal: census.leak_problems reports a new_rows url that carries a user:password@ part, naming the field and never the value

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools")
import census
pw="Hunter2"*2
def probs(u):return census.leak_problems({"outcomes":[],"gaps":[],"conflicts":[],"new_rows":[{"url":u,"title":"t","publisher":"p","licence":"l"}]})
a=probs("https://deploy:"+pw+"@example.org/a")
b=probs("http://deploy:"+pw+"@srv01.corp.contoso.com/a")
c=probs("https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/overview")
print("password urls:",a,b,"| clean url:",c)
sys.exit(0 if a and b and not c and "new_rows[0] url" in a[0] and "new_rows[0] url" in b[0] and pw not in " ".join(a+b) else 1)

clauses.clause: census.leak_problems reports a new_rows url that carries a user:password@ part, naming the field and never the value

notes: Planner 2026-10-26: repro and check 0 fail on main (https://deploy:<pw>@example.org/a gives no problem; the same with a corp host is reported only as an email hit, by the email rule, not as a url credential). kbcommon.url_holds_credential(url) already says whether a repository url carries user:password@ (and, for http and https, a bare user@ part); reuse it in the url branch of leak_problems with its own kind name. Check 0 also asserts the value is never printed and a clean url gives none.
